title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: A guard that changed job, now held in place
summary: Protects a guard that had quietly become a speed guard, and puts the check that found the last two navigation bugs into the suite.

highlights.title: A Rule That Became A Speed Guard
highlights.description: A rule added to fix wrong navigation is now redundant for that, but keeps parameter type clicks off the slower path: 42 percent faster on a real project. A check now holds it there, since no correctness test would miss it.

sections.heading: Internal
bullets: The rule that tells a type annotation from a named argument was added two releases ago to stop Ctrl+click going to the wrong place. The release after it made that wrong place unreachable by another route, so every correctness check now passes without the rule.

It is not dead though: it keeps a click on a parameter type out of the slower path. On a real project, 928 clicks of that shape open no file and take 75.8 ms with it, against 1388 file reads and 130.3 ms without. A check now holds it there, with a companion proving a real named argument still takes the slower path, so neither can pass by doing nothing.

The sweep that found both navigation bugs is now part of the suite: every identifier of a sample of a real project is clicked and the line reached must contain the word. It reports 14224 correct landings and none wrong, against 616 suspicious before the two fixes.
Clicks on a declaration, import aliases and companion objects are counted apart, being right for reasons that rule cannot see.

sections.heading: Notes
bullets: No behaviour change in this release.
